input.question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?
input.ground_truth: Let's start by differentiating between thirsty and dehydration. Thirst is wanting water, dehydration is running out of water. At later stage dehydration your renal system shuts down and waste backs up. You eventually die. You pee because you're using water to get rid of bad stuff in your system, not because you have too much water.

Question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a big water balloon. Inside your body, there is some water and also some stuff your body doesn’t need anymore, like extra salt and waste. 

When you drink water, your body fills up like a balloon. But even if you don’t drink water (when you’re thirsty or dehydrated), your body still makes a little bit of water inside, and it still needs to get rid of the waste and extra stuff.

So, your body uses a little bit of water to help get rid of the waste by making pee (urine). That’s why you still pee even when you’re thirsty or haven’t had any water. Your body wants to keep you clean inside!

But, if you don’t drink water, your pee will be darker and you’ll make less of it, because your body wants to keep as much water as it can for you.
